contract_plain_english: In the corrected nondegenerate very-sparse regime, where the expected degree stays between two positive constants while p may vary with n, a sufficiently large Erdős–Rényi graph has probability at least 0.9 of containing some vertex whose degree is at least a positive constant times log n/log log n.

source_evidence.observation: The source defines G(n,p) on n vertices by including each edge between distinct vertices independently with probability p, defines a vertex degree as its number of incident edges, and defines the expected degree by d=(n−1)p.

source_evidence.observation: The source declares that throughout the following exercises n grows to infinity and p is not assumed constant in n, so d may also vary with n.

source_evidence.observation: The source describes the regime as d=O(1), says the next exercise supplies a lower bound matching the O(log n/log log n) upper bound from Exercise 2.4.3, and asks for probability 0.9 that some vertex has degree Ω(log n/log log n).
The claimed lower-bound scale is log n divided by log log n, with a positive constant suppressed by Ω notation.

binders: A sequence of integers n tending to infinity.
A sequence of connection probabilities p=p(n) in [0,1].
Random graphs G_n distributed as G(n,p(n)).
Positive constants c_- and c_+ independent of n.
conclusions: There is a constant c>0 and a threshold N such that, for every n≥N, the probability that G_n has a vertex of degree at least c log n/log log n is at least 0.9.
definitions_and_conventions: In G(n,p), every unordered pair of distinct vertices is connected independently with probability p.
The degree of a vertex is the number of incident edges.
The notation Ω(log n/log log n) denotes a lower bound by a positive constant multiple of log n/log log n for all sufficiently large n.
The correction replaces the printed upper-bound-only condition d=O(1) by the nondegenerate very-sparse regime d=Θ(1).
hypotheses: For all sufficiently large n, c_- ≤ d_n ≤ c_+; equivalently, the expected-degree sequence is bounded above and bounded away from zero, d_n=Θ(1).
implicit_context: The asymptotic variable is the graph size n.
The probability is over the independent random edges of G_n.
The connection probability p may depend on n.
The base of the logarithm does not affect the asserted asymptotic order.

details: The upper bound d_n=O(1) is retained.
A positive eventual lower bound on d_n is added to exclude vanishing expected-degree sequences.
The event is existential over vertices: the maximum vertex degree reaches the stated scale.
The displayed probability threshold is 0.9 for all sufficiently large n.
The lower bound must use a strictly positive constant multiplier.
The multiplier is independent of n.

undebatable_constraints: The graph model must be G(n,p) with independent edges and expected degree d=(n−1)p.
The connection probability must be allowed to depend on n.
The conclusion must concern the existence of at least one vertex, not every vertex or a fixed vertex.
The degree threshold must have order log n/log log n with a positive multiplier.
The probability guarantee must be at least 0.9 for all sufficiently large n.
A valid correction must exclude sequences with d_n tending to zero; d_n=O(1) alone does not do so.
